gap: No result ChatGPT got states that at the 8.3 kWh size BLUETTI sells the panels and the SolarX 4K controller in separate bundles: the Apex 300 + 2× B300K + 2× 500 W kit page footnotes its 4,000 W solar figure with "Requires a SolarX 4K", and the bundle that includes the SolarX 4K ($4,498) has no panels.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages (StormWatts 240 V solar-input comparison, Solar Waypoint three-way comparison, EnergySage best solar generators) and the top result of the second chat (StormWatts kits at the same panel watts). EnergySage already says the Apex 300 takes 2,400 W, "more with SolarX 4K", and that it is AC-only without an add-on hub. StormWatts already gives the Apex 300's two native 1,200 W inputs, the port voltage and current windows for the Jackery 5000 Plus, Anker S5000, DELTA Pro 3 and F3800 Plus, and Jackery's two-panel limit for the SolarSaga 500 X. What they lack is which BLUETTI listing contains which part, the Jackery battery-pack count and exclusivity, and the store's mislabelled battery size on the 2× 200 W kit. The stronger finding I aimed for (how many 500 W panels each native Apex 300 input accepts, from BLUETTI's manual) could not be sourced, so this stays at 1.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. The two linked kits inside the size band are both Apex 300 + 2× B300K (8,294.4 Wh), and both are pre-orders for late January. The 2× 500 W kit is the one to prefer of the two; BLUETTI's page ties the 4,000 W solar figure to a SolarX 4K that this kit does not contain. Jackery's 5000 Plus was also a pre-order today (ships Dec 2, 500 X panel by Dec 5), so I found no kit in the band that ships now.
